newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate falls to 7.6 vs 8.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate falls to 7.6 vs 8.7 pct.

text.p: The average price of money fell to 7.6 percent on Thursday from 8.7 percent as key lenders kept rates flat in thin trade.
Because of very low demand for fresh funds, total loans on Zagreb's money market shrank to 11.5 million kuna from 20 million. Some 98 million kuna were offered.
Interbank call money was unchanged at eight percent, and the rate for short-term insurance firms' loans was seven percent.
Only 36.6 million kuna were settled in Wednesday's overnight trade as two banks borrowed money to square positions.

The central bank said it had no foreign exchange operations today. The kuna midrate for Friday firmed to 5.2682 from 5.2729 to the dollar while easing slightly to 3.5567 against the mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, 385-1-4557075
